title: Sorting & Search Journey
description: Merging, partitioning, binary-search boundaries, rotated arrays, matrices, and answer-space search.

journey.outcome: Maintain explicit partition and search-boundary invariants, then recognize when the answer space itself is monotonic.

connections.merge-sorted-array: Start by combining already sorted sequences. Writing backward avoids overwriting unread values when the first array also supplies the output buffer.
connections.merge-sort: Reuse merging after recursively sorting two halves. The merge invariant becomes the combine step of a divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm.
connections.sort-colors: Instead of merging, maintain regions with known membership. Three-way partitioning teaches exactly which section is processed and which positions still need inspection.
connections.quick-sort: Generalize partitioning around a pivot and recursively solve its remaining regions. Balanced partitions give good average behavior, while pivot choice and duplicates affect the worst case.
connections.kth-largest-element-in-an-array: Partitioning can select a rank without sorting both sides. Compare quickselect's one-sided recursion with the bounded-heap approach used in the Heap Journey.
connections.binary-search: Sorted order now lets an unsuccessful comparison discard half the candidates. Choose an interval convention and prove every update makes that interval smaller.
connections.search-insert-position: Change exact search into finding the first value at least the target. The insertion boundary still exists when the target itself is absent.
connections.find-first-and-last-position-of-element-: Reuse boundary search twice for duplicates: once for the first value at least the target and once for the first value strictly greater than it.
connections.sqrtx: Search an implicit sorted sequence of candidate roots. The answer is the final candidate whose square does not exceed the input, with overflow-safe comparisons.
connections.search-in-rotated-sorted-array: Global ordering is broken at one pivot, but one half remains sorted. Identify that half before deciding whether the target can lie inside it.
connections.find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array: Reuse the rotation structure without a target value. Comparing the middle with the right boundary reveals which side still contains the minimum.
connections.find-peak-element: A whole array need not be sorted for a directional search. An upward slope guarantees some peak to the right, while a downward slope preserves a peak on the left side.
connections.search-a-2d-matrix: Flatten coordinates conceptually when each row starts after the previous row ends. That stronger ordering permits ordinary binary search over a virtual one-dimensional array.
connections.search-a-2d-matrix-ii: Remove the cross-row ordering guarantee while retaining sorted rows and columns. A corner comparison can eliminate one row or column, but flattening is no longer a valid binary-search reduction.
connections.koko-eating-bananas: Search a possible answer rather than an input position. Feasibility becomes monotonic in eating speed, so find the smallest speed that meets the time budget.
connections.book-allocation-problem: Reuse binary search on the answer with a more involved feasibility scan. A proposed maximum load is valid only if contiguous books can be assigned within the allowed number of students.
connections.median-of-two-sorted-arrays: Interview stretch: binary-search a partition in the smaller array. Its partner partition is determined by the required left-half size, and cross-boundary inequalities certify the median.
connections.cses-1646: Start range-query preprocessing with an immutable array. Prefix totals turn each inclusive interval sum into a difference between two already computed boundaries.
connections.cses-1648: Optional interview stretch: point assignments make rebuilding all prefix totals too expensive. A Fenwick tree updates and queries logarithmically by storing reusable binary-sized prefix blocks.
connections.cses-1649: Optional interview stretch: minimum cannot be recovered by subtracting prefix minima. A segment tree combines disjoint interval summaries and recomputes only the ancestors affected by a point update.

topics.name: Merging, partitioning, and selection
topics.description: Build sorting from a combine step or partition invariant, then avoid unnecessary sorting for a rank query.

topics.name: Binary-search boundaries
topics.description: Separate exact matches, insertion points, duplicate ranges, and final feasible candidates.

topics.name: Structured search spaces
topics.description: Identify which ordering guarantee remains before deciding what a comparison can eliminate.

topics.name: Answer-space and partition search
topics.description: Prove feasibility is monotonic and use it to search capacities, rates, or balanced partitions.
